info.name: CompositeFX
info.comment: Composite two sources together with a mixing algorithm.

description.p: This filter combines the FilterEffect.Input and FilterEffect.Mix sources using either one of the Porter-Duff compositing operations, or a colour blending algorithm. The Input has priority and will be placed in the foreground for ordered operations such as ATOP and OVER.

action.name: Draw
action.comment: Render the effect to the target bitmap.
action.prototype: ERR acDraw(*Object, DOUBLE X, DOUBLE Y, DOUBLE Width, DOUBLE Height)

input.param: The X position of the region to be drawn.
The Y position of the region to be drawn.
The width of the region to be drawn.
The height of the region to be drawn.

description.p: The Amount interpolates between the FilterEffect.Mix source and the fully composited result. A value of 1, the default, gives the unmodified result of the Operator and a value of 0 passes the Mix source through unchanged. Intermediate values blend the two with premultiplied components in the effect's colour space, so the alpha of the result is also interpolated. The Amount applies to every operator, including ARITHMETIC.
The value must be in the range 0 - 1. Values outside of this range, or that are not finite, are rejected with ERR::InvalidValue. If an AmountMask is bound then it scales the Amount for each pixel.
SVG documents can set this field with the kotuku:amount attribute of feComposite and feBlend.

field.name: AmountMask
field.comment: Optional earlier effect whose output scales Amount.

description.p: Bind an earlier effect in the same filter to vary the Amount across the image. The mask is aligned with the scene and sampled at each output pixel, and the sampled value multiplies Amount for that pixel. Where the mask is 1 the composited result is used at full Amount, and where it is 0 the FilterEffect.Mix source passes through unchanged.

The value is read from the alpha channel of an image result, as stored and without colour conversion. A producer with a numerical result supplies the value directly. Values are limited to the range 0 - 1. Pixels outside of the producer's result read as 0. The mask does not contribute to the default primitive subregion, and it is not read while Amount is 0.
Attach both effects to the same filter before setting this field. If the producer is removed, this field is cleared and the mask no longer applies. Set the field to NULL to remove the mask.
SVG documents can set this field with the kotuku:amountMask attribute of feComposite and feBlend, which names the result of an earlier primitive.

field.name: K1
field.comment: Input value for the arithmetic operation.

description.p: The ARITHMETIC operator computes result = K1 * i1 * i2 + K2 * i1 + K3 * i2 + K4 for each premultiplied colour component, where i1 is the FilterEffect.Input and i2 is the FilterEffect.Mix.

field.name: K2
field.comment: Input value for the arithmetic operation.

description.p: Refer to K1 for the arithmetic formula.

field.name: K3
field.comment: Input value for the arithmetic operation.

description.p: Refer to K1 for the arithmetic formula.

field.name: K4
field.comment: Input value for the arithmetic operation.

description.p: Refer to K1 for the arithmetic formula.

field.name: Operator
field.comment: The compositing algorithm to use for rendering.

description.p: Setting the Operator will determine the algorithm that is used for compositing. The default is OVER.
Operators that mix colour components use FilterEffect.ColourSpace. They inherit the parent VectorFilter's colour space by default. The IN and OUT operators only modify the alpha channel.

field.name: XMLDef
field.comment: Describes the primitive using the FilterEffect.XMLDef format.

constants.const: The SVG 'arithmetic' blending algorithm.
The Porter-Duff 'atop' operator; the mix alpha channel has priority and the input channel does not occlude.
Gives a darker result than MULTIPLY by increasing the contrast between the input and mix colours.
Adjust the mix contrast using the input colour values as the contrast strength.
Use the darker colour components of the mix and input values.
Output the difference between the input and mix colours.
Gives a brighter result than SCREEN by decreasing the contrast between the input and mix colours.
Produce the difference between the mix and input values around a reference point of mid-grey.
Apply MULTIPLY or SCREEN according to the input colour, producing a high-contrast result.
The Porter-Duff 'in' operator; the input alpha channel has priority and the mix channel is secondary.
Invert the mix colour components using the input alpha channel as the strength.
Invert the mix colour components using the input colour channels as the per-channel strength.
Use the lighter colour components of the mix and input values.
The input colour value is subtracted from the mix.
Multiplies the input and mix colour components, producing a darker result unless one source is white.
The Porter-Duff 'out' operator; the mix alpha channel is inversed with the input channel.
The Porter-Duff 'over' operator, this is the default operation for standard alpha blending.
Combines the multiply and screen blend modes, with the mix determining tonal strength.
Add the input and mix colour values together.
Produces a result brighter than the input.
Apply a softer variant of HARD_LIGHT, subtly darkening or lightening the mix from the input colour.
The Porter-Duff 'xor' operator; blend as normal but occlusion occurs when input and mix alpha channels interact.
